entry.title: Registration keys
entry.summary: - Every instance needs a free registration key. The key must fit the Salesforce org's kind: production, sandbox or Developer Edition. It is verified inside the instance, so it needs no network. See Registration keys. - A License panel in Settings to save or remove the key, see its state, and paste a status token from CloudAlgo by hand. LICENSE_KEY sets the key from the environment instead. - Sync pauses, nothing fails. A missing, wrong-kind, suspended or expired license holds back all Salesforce work; jobs complete and no change is lost. Alerts, the algobridge_license_state metric and the lice

entry.title: Alerts, webhooks, the API and Settings
entry.summary: - Alerts on their own screen and by email, through your SMTP server. - Webhooks: signed events about alerts, mappings and connections, sent to endpoints you add. - An audit log of console actions. - The /api/v1 API with access tokens, and configuration as code for mappings. - Schema drift checks that notice when a mapped field or column changes on either side. - A status page, metrics and a Settings page for instance settings.

entry.title: 0.9.0-rc.1
entry.summary: - The first release candidate. AlgoBridge now has a version number, and each release is a container image, ghcr.io/cloudalgo/algobridge, built for amd64 and arm64. Release candidates are for testing and are not public; the first public release comes later. - Install from a pinned image. The reference Compose file pulls the release you name in deploy/.env instead of building from source, and never uses latest. See Install. - Signed and scanned. Every image is signed, checked for critical vulnerabilities before release, and carries a software bill of materials. See Verify the image.

entry.title: Change notifier
entry.summary: - Push notifications from Salesforce. Record-triggered Flows tell AlgoBridge which objects changed, so it learns about changes without spending API calls. Notifications carry object names only, never record data. See Change notifier. - One-click pairing between the instance and the org, at a cost of 2 API calls, with key rotation and an instant revoke. - Signed requests. Every notification is signed and checked for key, org, timestamp, replay and rate. Repeated failed requests open an alert. - A slow fallback poll, hourly by default, catches anything a notification missed. - Your own saves are

entry.title: Apex probe and change sources
entry.summary: - The Apex bundle. A small, read-only Apex package you can deploy to your org from the console. It answers "has anything changed?" for up to 90 objects in one API call, against 5 per call without it. - Choose your change source: Composite (the default, nothing to install), Apex probe or change notifier. AlgoBridge verifies your choice before saving it, re-checks it daily, and falls back with an alert if it stops working. See Change sources.

entry.title: Live log
entry.summary: - A real-time view of every process's log lines in the console, for administrators. Follow, pause, filter and copy. Nothing is stored; the log streams only while someone is watching. See Live log. - Clearer SSO refusals. When an identity provider refuses a sign-in, the log now records the provider's error code.

entry.title: Initial load, Reload and the daily sweep
entry.summary: - Initial load of every record when you activate a mapping, over REST or Bulk API, whichever costs fewer calls, with progress on the console. - Reload empties a table and loads it again. You confirm it by typing the table name. - Daily reconciliation sweep removes rows Salesforce no longer has and repairs rows that differ. It refuses to delete a large share of a table at once. - Outbound sends on a latency bound: a batch goes when 200 changes are waiting or the oldest has waited the maximum wait. - Formula fields are blocked from sync, because polling cannot keep them correct.

entry.title: API budget governor and adaptive intervals
entry.summary: - Soft and hard thresholds for the org's API usage. Above the soft threshold AlgoBridge slows down; above the hard threshold it pauses Salesforce calls, while changes keep queuing. See API budget. - Adaptive poll intervals. A quiet object is polled less often, and a busy one returns to its minimum interval.

entry.title: Salesforce to PostgreSQL sync
entry.summary: - Change probes that check 5 objects per API call before reading anything. - Fetch and apply of changed records, matched on sfid and then on External ID, including deletes. - Conflict policies per mapping: sf_wins, pg_wins and latest_wins. See Conflicts.

entry.title: PostgreSQL to Salesforce sync, Bulk API and Activity
entry.summary: - Writes to Salesforce over SOAP, 200 records per call, sending only changed fields, with the new sfid written back to your row. - Bulk API v2 for runs of 2,000 records or more. - Retries with backoff for rejected changes; failures are parked rather than lost. - The Activity screen: every change in both directions, with filters, record detail and Salesforce's error text. Retry or discard a failed change, or retry all failures.

entry.title: Provisioning
entry.summary: - Tables built for you. AlgoBridge creates and extends mapped tables, the change log and the capture trigger in your database. - Additive changes only. It never drops or recreates a table, and it refuses a change that would narrow a column. - You stay in control. Every change is shown as a diff and runs only when you press Apply. A preflight check names any missing database grant.

entry.title: Mappings
entry.summary: - Map Salesforce objects to tables: choose fields, set direction (read-only or read-write), pick an External ID, add reference fields. - Choose a write algorithm: Ordered or Merged.

entry.title: Job runner
entry.summary: - Background jobs coordinated entirely in PostgreSQL, with a worker registry, automatic takeover when a worker stops, and a watchdog that restarts stalled schedules. - The Jobs and workers screen. See Workers and jobs.

entry.title: Salesforce connection
entry.summary: - Connect your org through an External Client App, using OAuth with PKCE against your My Domain. Tokens are stored encrypted. - API usage at a glance. The connection screen shows the org's API usage and AlgoBridge's own share. See Salesforce connection.

entry.title: Client database connection
entry.summary: - Connect your PostgreSQL from the console or with CLIENT_DATABASE_URL. The connection string is stored encrypted. See Client database. - Encrypted secrets with key rotation, through the rotate-encryption-key command. - A setup checklist on the dashboard.

entry.title: Single sign-on, form protection and user management
entry.summary: - Single sign-on through OpenID Connect, with presets for Google Workspace and Microsoft Entra ID and a generic option for other providers. Optional sign-up by email domain, and a setting to require SSO. See Single sign-on. - Every form is protected by a signed token and a one-time key, so forged and double submissions are refused. - User management: invitations, role changes, disabling users and admin-issued password-reset links, with optional email over SMTP. See Users and roles.

entry.title: Foundation, sign-in and console shell
entry.summary: - One container image that runs as console, worker or both, with health endpoints and a migrate command. - Local sign-in with argon2id passwords, optional two-step verification and account lockout. - Three roles (viewer, member, admin), with every route denied unless it names the permission it needs. - The console shell and the create-admin command for the first administrator.
